relations.definition: Indicates that a prize or amount is given to a recipient.
relations.embedding_query_text: awarded to: Indicates that a prize or amount is given to a recipient.

instances: US Open prize money -> men's singles
US Open prize money -> women's singles

chosen_property.label: awardedTo
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the recipient of a prize or award.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property expresses PrizeAward to recipient; award is inverse (entity to award text).

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: recipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An educational credential awarded relation between a course or program and the credential received upon successful completion. Also called "award received", "qualification granted", "certificate earned". Examples: "Course 'Introduction to Python' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program 'MBA' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Master of Business Administration'", "Training 'First Aid' educationalCredentialAwarded 'First Aid Certification'".

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

candidates.label: fundedItem
candidates.comment: A funded item relation between a grant and the biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product that receives direct or indirect funding or sponsorship. Also called: grant recipient, sponsored item, supported entity. Examples: "Research Grant" funded item "Cancer Research Project", "Arts Grant" funded item "Local Theater Production", "Educational Grant" funded item "Student Scholarship Program". Distinct from funding, which is the grant itself.

candidates.label: amount
candidates.comment: An amount relation between a financial entity (e.g., loan, grant, money transfer) and the monetary value or number associated with it. Also called value, sum, quantity of money. Examples: "A loan's amount is '$10,000'.", "The grant's amount is '€5,000'.", "A money transfer's amount is '250'."

candidates.label: ccRecipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation for a message, indicating a contact point, organization, or person who is copied on it. Also called "carbon copy recipient", "copied to", "CC'd party". Examples: "Email message ccRecipient John Doe", "Internal memo message ccRecipient HR Department".

candidates.label: beneficiaryBank
candidates.comment: A bank, branch, or financial institution operating the beneficiary's bank account or releasing funds for a money transfer. Also called: recipient bank, receiving bank, destination bank. Examples: "MoneyTransfer 'Wire Transfer' beneficiaryBank 'Bank of America'", "MoneyTransfer 'International Transfer' beneficiaryBank 'HSBC'."

candidates.label: borrower
candidates.comment: A person who borrows the object being lent in a lend action. Also called: recipient of loan, loan taker. Examples: "LendAction 'Book Loan' borrower 'Jane Doe'", "LendAction 'Tool Rental' borrower 'John Smith'". Distinct from lender, which is the person providing the object.

relations.definition: Specifies the monetary value associated with an event or item.
relations.embedding_query_text: amount: Specifies the monetary value associated with an event or item.

candidates.label: amount
candidates.comment: An amount relation between a financial entity (e.g., loan, grant, money transfer) and the monetary value or number associated with it. Also called value, sum, quantity of money. Examples: "A loan's amount is '$10,000'.", "The grant's amount is '€5,000'.", "A money transfer's amount is '250'."

candidates.label: price
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the monetary value of an offer, product, or price component. Also called cost, rate, charge, amount. Examples: An offer has a price of '19.99'. A product has a price of '100'. The service has a price of '50.00'. Distinct from priceCurrency, which specifies the currency of the price.

candidates.label: value
candidates.comment: A value relation between a monetary amount, property value, or quantitative value and its specific numerical, textual, boolean, or structured content. Also called amount, quantity, content. Examples: "QuantitativeValue value '10'", "PropertyValue value 'red'", "MonetaryAmount value '99.99'".

candidates.label: amountOfThisGood
candidates.comment: An amount of this good relation between a type and quantity node and the numerical quantity of a specific good included in an offer. Also called quantity, number of items, item count. Examples: "A shopping cart item's amount of this good is '2'.", "The offer specifies an amount of this good as '5'."

candidates.label: returnShippingFeesAmount
candidates.comment: The monetary cost associated with shipping products back for returns. Also called return shipping cost, return postage fee, shipping fee for returns. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$7.99"`, `Large Item Return Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$25.00"`, `Free Returns Policy` returnShippingFeesAmount `"$0.00"`. Distinct from `returnFees`, which specifies the *type* of fee, not the amount.

candidates.label: orderQuantity
candidates.comment: The number or quantity of a specific item ordered within an order item. Also called item quantity, ordered amount, number of units. Examples: "OrderItem A orderQuantity 2", "OrderItem B orderQuantity 5", "OrderItem C orderQuantity 1". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on total items for shipping.

candidates.label: maxValue
candidates.comment: An upper value relation between a monetary amount, property value, property value specification, or quantitative value and the highest value of a characteristic or property. Also called: maximum limit, upper bound, highest possible value. Examples: "Temperature Range maxValue 30", "Age Limit maxValue 65", "Credit Score maxValue 850". Distinct from maxPrice, which specifically refers to the highest price in a range.

candidates.label: baseSalary
candidates.comment: A monetary amount, number, or price specification representing the base salary of a job or an employee role. Also called: starting salary, basic pay, compensation. Examples: "JobPosting 'Software Engineer' baseSalary '$120,000'", "EmployeeRole 'Manager' baseSalary 'MonetaryAmount 80000 USD'."

candidates.label: currency
candidates.comment: A monetary unit relation between a monetary amount or specification and the currency in which it is expressed. Also called: monetary currency, unit of money, payment unit. Examples: "Product Price" currency "USD", "Loan Amount" currency "EUR", "Exchange Rate" currency "JPY", "Salary" currency "GBP". Distinct from costCurrency, which is specific to drug costs.

candidates.label: loanPaymentAmount
candidates.comment: A payment amount relation between a repayment specification and the monetary amount of a single payment. Also called: single payment amount, installment amount, payment value. Examples: "Monthly Repayment loanPaymentAmount $1,500", "Quarterly Installment loanPaymentAmount €750", "Final Payment loanPaymentAmount £10,000".

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: parentService
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a broadcast service and a broader broadcast service it is a variation or component of. Also called belongs to, is a variation of, is part of, is a channel of. Examples: BBC One Scotland is a parent service of BBC One. A regional news channel is a parent service of a national news channel. A specific sports channel is a parent service of a broader sports network.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

relations.definition: Indicates the place where an entity is situated.
relations.embedding_query_text: located in: Indicates the place where an entity is situated.

instances: US Open prize money -> New York

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: address
candidates.comment: An address relation between an entity (e.g., organization, person, place) and its physical postal address. Also called physical location, mailing address, street address. Examples: "A company's address is '123 Main St, Anytown'.", "A person's address is 'PO Box 123'.", "The restaurant's address is '456 Oak Ave'."

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: isLocatedInSubcellularLocation
candidates.comment: A subcellular localization relation between a biochemical entity and its specific location within a cell. Also called found in subcellular location, localized to, present in subcellular compartment. Examples: A protein is isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'cytoplasm'. DNA is isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'nucleus'. Mitochondrial enzymes are isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'mitochondrion'.

candidates.label: globalLocationNumber
candidates.comment: A global location number relation between an organization, person, or place and its unique 13-digit GLN identifier. Also called: GLN, International Location Number, ILN. Examples: "Acme Corp Warehouse" global location number "1234567890123", "Hospital Main Campus" global location number "9876543210987", "Distribution Center X" global location number "1122334455667".

candidates.label: totalPaymentDue

candidates.label: netWorth
candidates.comment: The total financial value of a person, calculated as assets minus liabilities. Also called personal wealth, financial worth, total assets. Examples: "Person A netWorth '$1,000,000'", "Person B netWorth '$500,000'", "Person C netWorth '$10,000'".

candidates.label: maximumAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: An attendee capacity relation between an event or place and the total number of individuals it can accommodate. Also called: maximum occupancy, total capacity, attendee limit. candidates.label: offerCount

candidates.label: price

candidates.label: downPayment
candidates.comment: A down payment relation between a repayment specification and a monetary amount or number, representing an initial payment made at the start of a purchase. Examples: "Car loan repayment downPayment '$5000'", "House purchase repayment downPayment '10% of total'", "Furniture financing downPayment '200 USD'".

candidates.label: totalPrice
candidates.comment: A total price relation between a reservation or ticket and its full cost, including taxes and shipping. Also called full cost, final price, reservation cost. Examples: "Reservation totalPrice '$120.00'", "Ticket totalPrice '€50.00'", "Flight reservation totalPrice '$350.75'".

candidates.label: value

candidates.label: healthPlanCostSharing

candidates.label: ccRecipient

candidates.label: sharedContent

Examples: `Social Media Post` sharedContent `ImageObject: Photo of event`, `Blog Comment` sharedContent `VideoObject: YouTube link`, `Forum Post` sharedContent `AudioObject: Podcast snippet`. Distinct from `mentions`, which is a reference to another entity, not necessarily embedded content.

candidates.label: commentCount
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".

candidates.label: greaterOrEqual
candidates.comment: A greater or equal relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior to or the same as another. Also called: is greater than or equal to, at least, no less than. Examples: "High" greater or equal "Medium", "Good" greater or equal "Good", "Large" greater or equal "Medium". Distinct from greater, which does not include equality.

candidates.label: greater
candidates.comment: A greater relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior or larger than another. Also called: is greater than, exceeds, is more than. Examples: "High" greater "Medium", "Excellent" greater "Good", "Large" greater "Small". Distinct from greaterOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: equal
candidates.comment: An equality relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject qualitative value is considered equal to the object qualitative value within a specific ordering context. Also called "is equivalent to", "is the same as", "matches". Examples: "Qualitative value 'Satisfactory' equal 'Acceptable'", "Qualitative value 'Medium' equal 'Average'", "Qualitative value 'High' equal 'Very Good'".

candidates.label: valueReference
candidates.comment: A value reference relation between a property value, qualitative value, or quantitative value and a secondary value providing additional information or context. Also called reference value, contextual value, measurement context. Examples: "QuantitativeValue valueReference 'Standard Temperature'", "PropertyValue valueReference 'Color Spectrum'", "QuantitativeValue valueReference 'RPM at max torque'".

candidates.label: currentExchangeRate

candidates.label: stepValue
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the required granularity or increment for a property value specification. Also called "granularity", "increment value", "step size", "value interval". Examples: "The slider has stepValue 1", "The input field's stepValue is 0.5", "This property requires a stepValue of 10."

candidates.label: value
candidates.comment: A value relation between a monetary amount, property value, or quantitative value and its specific numerical, textual, boolean, or structured content. candidates.label: maxValue

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
